clue: Snail-shaped part of the inner ear.
why: The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear that turns sound vibrations into nerve signals.
pearl: Uncoiled, the human cochlea is only about 3.5 cm long.

clue: Tough cord that joins muscle to bone.
why: Tendons transmit the pull of a muscle to a bone. Ligaments, by contrast, join bone to bone.
pearl: The Achilles is the thickest and strongest tendon in the body.

clue: Temporary organ that feeds a growing baby.
why: The placenta passes oxygen and nutrients from the pregnant person to the fetus and carries waste away.
pearl: It is the only organ the body grows from scratch and then discards, and most of it develops from the embryo’s own cells.

clue: 206 bones, give or take. Tonight’s star decoration.
why: The adult skeleton has about 206 bones. It supports and protects the body, anchors muscles and makes blood cells in the marrow.
pearl: Babies are born with around 300 bones or bony parts. Many fuse as they grow.
